stem: A piecewise function g is defined as: g(x) = 2x + 3 when x < 1, g(1) = 7, and g(x) = x^2 + 4 when x > 1. Which of the following correctly describes the behaviour of g at x = 1?

options.text: g is continuous at x = 1 because g(1) is defined
g is continuous at x = 1 because the left-hand limit equals the right-hand limit
g is discontinuous at x = 1 because the left-hand limit (5) does not equal g(1) = 7 even though both one-sided limits are equal
g is discontinuous at x = 1 because the left-hand limit does not exist

per_option_rationale.rationale: Checks only whether g(1) is defined (it is, equals 7) and ignores whether the limit of g equals that value.

LHL = lim(x->1-) (2x+3) = 5 and RHL = lim(x->1+) (x^2+4) = 5; the two limits are indeed equal, but continuity also requires the limit to equal g(1) = 7, which it does not. Stops short at one condition.

LHL = 2(1)+3 = 5. RHL = 1^2+4 = 5. So the two-sided limit = 5. But g(1) = 7, which is not 5. All of f(a) defined, limit exists, but limit is not equal to f(a), so g is discontinuous at x = 1 (a removable discontinuity).
Incorrectly claims the left-hand limit does not exist; lim(x->1-) (2x+3) = 2(1)+3 = 5, which is well-defined.

explanation: Both one-sided limits equal 5 so the two-sided limit exists, but g(1) = 7 is not equal to 5, making x = 1 a removable discontinuity.

explanation_sections.punchline: The two-sided limit exists and equals 5, but g(1) = 7 is not equal to 5, so the third continuity condition fails.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: check continuity conditions one by one. (1) g(1) = 7 is defined. (2) LHL = 2(1)+3 = 5; RHL = 1^2+4 = 5; limit exists and equals 5. (3) Limit (5) is not equal to g(1) (7). Condition 3 fails, so g is discontinuous. This is a removable discontinuity repairable by setting g(1) = 5.
explanation_sections.lesson: Even when both one-sided limits agree, continuity fails if the function value at the point does not equal that limit.
explanation_sections.timing: 75-90 seconds. Two substitutions take 20 seconds. Trap: option 2 is seductive because the one-sided limits do agree.
